uncited: This family defines three specific architectural configurations for the FWD framework, distinguished by their depth supervision strategy and the initialization state of the depth estimation module.
They address the trade-off between training stability, convergence speed, and reliance on external geometric priors.
FWD-U serves as the unsupervised baseline, FWD provides a supervised baseline with pre-trained geometry, and FWD-D bypasses learned depth estimation entirely by using sensor data.
All variants in this family operate within the FWD (Forward Warping and Depth) framework for real-time novel view synthesis.
The primary divergence lies in how the depth map is obtained and whether the depth estimation network is trainable during the end-to-end optimization loop.
FWD-U is the unsupervised variant of the model.
This variant is chosen when no external depth priors or pre-trained models are available, serving as a baseline for unsupervised learning capabilities.
This approach leverages strong geometric priors from pre-training while allowing the depth estimator to adapt to the specific domain of the target scene.
It is chosen when faster convergence and higher geometric accuracy are required compared to the unsupervised variant.
FWD-D is a variant that eliminates the learned MVS module entirely.
Because sensor depths provide abundant and accurate geometry cues, no MVS network is used.
This variant is chosen when high-quality sensor data is available, offering the most robust geometric supervision without the error propagation risks of learned depth estimation.
The study highlights how the initialization of the depth estimator and the source of depth data impact the final synthesis quality and training dynamics.

This confirms that the PatchmatchNet weights are indeed updated during the end-to-end training process.

No pre-training on MVS datasets is performed, and the network learns depth representations solely through the photometric and perceptual losses inherent to the novel view synthesis task [S1].

The claim states that 'No pre-training on MVS datasets is performed' and that the network learns 'solely through the photometric and perceptual losses'. The evidence supports the first part for the specific variant FWD-U ('PatchmatchNet is randomly initialized without any pretraining'). However, the evidence explicitly states that for the FWD variant, 'PatchmatchNet [77] as the MVS module... is pretrained'. Furthermore, the text mentions 'For pretraining PatchmatchNet, we train it following typical MVS settings', indicating that pre-training on MVS datasets *is* performed for the base model. Therefore, the claim is not universally true for the method described, as it depends on the specific variant (FWD-U vs FWD). Additionally, the claim implies a general property of the method, but the evidence shows a supervised variant (FWD) exists which uses pre-training.

The evidence supports that the core mechanism involves depth estimation (for FWD/FWD-U) and warping, and that these variants share this approach.
